Team / Dana — thanks for the notes. I reviewed the CB redlines and Ben's counter. High-level legal position below — I tracked responses to each of the three issues you raised: 

1) Metering / Data visibility:
- Accept in principle: Redwood will provide daily machine-readable exports and API access. We will propose a "data reconciliation" section that defines the schema and the export cadence.

2) Passback timing SLA:
- Conditional accept: we will agree to a 48-hour target but include explicit exceptions for downstream reseller processing and force majeure. Also propose a service-level definition: "reporting" means the actionable reconciliation file is made available to CloudBridge or pushed to CloudBridge's bucket.

3) Liability carve-out for billing errors:
- Limited accept: Redwood will accept an adjustment/credit remedy for verified billing errors discovered within a 30-day reconciliation window. We will not accept an open-ended customer refund obligation for third-party marketplace charges. Proposed language: 
  - "For verified billing errors related to Redwood-managed metering, Redwood's sole financial liability shall be limited to the adjustment of affected invoices and issuance of credits not to exceed the total invoiced amount for the applicable billing period."

Open legal asks for CloudBridge counsel:
- Please confirm whether a pooled cap (monthly) or per-incident cap is preferred.
- If you need a longer audit window, flag it now.

Happy to hop on a call. Ben / Karthik — I will consolidate a clean tracked-changes doc by EOD and attach.
